title: Beach Volleyball Tournament Poster
description: A promotional poster for a fictional beach volleyball tournament in the Town of Shelbyville, built entirely in Adobe Illustrator with every illustration and typographic element constructed as vector artwork for precise control over colour, scale, and composition.

title: Furrever Pals Puppy Yoga
description: A branding and service design project for a puppy yoga studio in Vancouver, built around a gap in existing local offerings: none combined wellness with shelter dog adoption. The project spans brand identity, visual design, and a fully hand coded website, connecting community wellbeing to animal welfare through one accessible experience.

title: MyBCIT Page Re-Design
description: A redesign of the MyBCIT student portal, built on interviews with over ten students, graduates, and first time users to identify what made the platform hard to navigate. The redesign reduces the clicks needed to reach core tasks like grades, while keeping BCIT's colour palette modern and immediately recognizable.

title: Boardwalk Boutique App Design
description: An app for a skate and streetwear rental shop, built with React Native around how people actually browse, book, and check out rentals. Boardwalk Boutique includes real time notifications and store location features to keep users oriented and informed throughout the rental process.

title: Bing: The Redesign
description: A redesign of Bing grounded in user research into how people actually search and where existing friction points slow them down. The redesign focuses on reducing clutter and surfacing more relevant results, making it faster for users to find what they need.

title: National Geographics Magazine Design
description: A fictional National Geographic magazine cover exploring the space between imagination and reality, composited in Photoshop from a mix of stock imagery and original illustration. Surreal elements, like a giraffe towering beside a mountain range, sit within an otherwise realistic composition, blurring the line between a real travel magazine and an imagined one.
